title: The weather is lovely
goal: Use adjectives correctly — and accept a surprising fact: 很 in front of an adjective often does NOT mean "very".
bekal: build adjective sentences without 是 and with an "empty" 很
compare two things with 比 and express sameness with 一樣
talk about the weather and seasons in Taiwan

dialogs.title: 對話 — 台南的天氣
dialogs.intro: First day in Tainan. Budi is surprised at how different it feels from Taipei.

notes: **又…又… means "both… and…"** for two qualities that come together: 又冷又濕 (cold and damp), 又便宜又好吃 (cheap and tasty). ⚠️ The two qualities must be of the same kind — both good, or both bad.
**差不多 ("the difference isn't much") means "about the same, roughly"** and is used constantly. It can also mean "that'll do": *差不多了* = "that's about enough, almost done".
⚠️ **怕 means "be afraid" and also "can't stand"**: 我怕熱 (I can't stand heat), 我怕辣 (I can't handle spicy food), 我怕冷 (I can't stand the cold). This form is very handy in restaurants.
**別 = 不要, but shorter and more casual**: 別擔心 (don't worry), 別客氣 (don't mention it), 別走 (don't go). In everyday speech, 別 and 不要 are equally common.
**超…的 is a young Taiwanese frame** for "so…, super…": 超熱的, 超好吃的, 超便宜的. Note the 的 at the end — without it, it sounds unfinished.

grammars.title: ⚠️ Adjectives: no 是, and a 很 that means nothing
body: This is the most common sticking point after measure words. In Mandarin, **adjectives behave like verbs**. They don't need 是 — and in return, they almost always need something in front of them, usually 很.
after: ⚠️ **In an ordinary sentence, 很 is almost empty of meaning.** It's just a prop that makes the sentence complete. If you really want to say "very", use **真** (really), **非常** (extremely), **太…了** (too), or **超** (super).
**Why 很 is needed:** an adjective with no prop sounds like an unfinished comparison. *我忙* feels like "I'm busy (and you're not)". Adding 很 makes it neutral.
⚠️ **很 disappears in negatives and questions**: *天氣不好* ✓, *天氣好嗎？* ✓ — not *天氣不很好* or *天氣很好嗎？*

grammars.title: 比 and 一樣: comparing
body: **A 比 B + adjective** = "A is more … than B". ⚠️ Note that **很 disappears** in comparisons — using it is a very common mistake.

head: Sentence
Pīnyīn
Meaning
rows: Tainan isn't as cold as Taipei.
Tainan is as hot as Taipei.

after: ⚠️ **The difference stands AFTER the adjective**, not before: *熱一點* (a bit hotter), *貴五十塊* (fifty dollars more expensive), *大兩歲* (two years older). English often puts it first ("a bit hotter"), and that habit tends to carry over.
**Negate a comparison with 沒有, not 不比**: *台南沒有台北冷* = "Tainan isn't as cold as Taipei". The form 不比 exists, but its meaning is narrower and beginners rarely need it.
**最 (*zuì*, most) stands right before the adjective**: 最好, 最貴, 最喜歡. It's one of the most frequent words in everyday conversation.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Two things you need to know about Taiwan
items: **颱風 (typhoons)** come between July and October, several times a year. When the government announces a **颱風假** (typhoon day off), schools and offices close — and all of Taiwan celebrates. ⚠️ Don't go out during a typhoon; flying objects are a real danger.

**地震 (earthquakes)** are frequent because Taiwan sits on a plate boundary. Small quakes happen almost weekly, and Taiwanese people don't react at all. What you need to know: take cover under a table; don't run outside.
**Useful sentences:** *今天有颱風嗎？* (is there a typhoon today?), *剛剛地震了！* (there was just an earthquake!), *你還好嗎？* (are you OK?).
Phones in Taiwan sound a loud alarm for earthquake and typhoon alerts. ⚠️ Don't turn those alerts off.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **好 placed before a verb makes an adjective**: 好吃 (tasty to eat), 好喝 (tasty to drink), 好看 (good-looking), 好玩 (fun), 好聽 (pleasant to hear). This pattern gives you dozens of free words. The opposite uses 難: 難吃 (tastes bad), 難看 (ugly), 難聽 (unpleasant to hear).

⚠️ Compare **有一點貴** and **便宜一點**. The first means "a bit expensive" (a complaint); the second means "a bit cheaper" (a request). The difference is position: **有一點 before** the adjective is a complaint; **一點 after** the adjective is a comparison. Put it in the wrong place and the meaning flips.

exercises.prompt: Fill in with 很, 比, 最, 一樣, or 太.
Put the words in the right order.
items: 熱 / 台北 / 台南 / 比
一樣 / 我 / 跟 / 他 / 高
最 / 這個 / 好 / 便宜

answers: 天氣很好。 — 我很忙。 — 台南比台北熱。 — 這個最便宜。 — 今天不熱。 — 跟印尼一樣。
我很忙。 — 天氣不好。 — 台南比台北熱。 — 這個貴嗎？ — 我二十歲。
很 — 比 — 很 — 太 — 一樣 — 很
天氣很好。 — 台南比台北熱。 — 太貴了。 — 我跟他一樣高。 — 這個最便宜。
